# Thereabouts dataset tables

## Dataset tables

Plain Parquet files, one directory per table. Partition labels in directory names (`country=XX`, `group=...`) are file routing, not columns. Observation tables keep duplicates; only the keys listed are guaranteed unique.

| Table | Grain | Key | Feeds packs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`airports`](#airports) | One row per airport record in the pinned OurAirports file; duplicate observations are retained. | `source`, `source_id` | `airports` |
| [`blocks`](#blocks) | One row per covered resolution 3 block, including blocks that store no cells. A block absent from this table is outside the coverage of this export. | `block` | none |
| [`canonical_cities`](#canonical_cities) | One row per canonical city or town; city_id is the place identifier of its anchor. | `city_id` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`cells`](#cells) | One row per stored H3 cell: a resolution 8 cell, or a coarser ancestor (resolution 3 to 7) that stands for all its resolution 8 descendants when they share one label. | `h3_uint64` | `core` |
| [`countries`](#countries) | One row per country or territory code in the pinned sources. | `country_code` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`ip_ranges`](#ip_ranges) | One row per published IP interval, from ip_start to ip_end inclusive. | `source`, `source_id` | `ip` |
| [`names`](#names) | One row per canonical city and distinct name. Names that fold to the same text, or to the city's canonical or English name, are kept once. | `city_id`, `name` | `core` |
| [`phone_metadata`](#phone_metadata) | One row per libphonenumber territory, including the non-geographic territory 001. | `source`, `source_id` | `phone` |
| [`phone_prefixes`](#phone_prefixes) | One row per prefix description in one language file, so a prefix repeats once per language. | `source`, `source_id` | `phone` |
| [`place_to_city`](#place_to_city) | One row per place; every places row has exactly one mapping row. | `place_id` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`places`](#places) | One row per reconciled place. | `place_id` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`plate_codes`](#plate_codes) | One row per source assertion of a code; a code repeats across sources, series and validity periods. | none | `plates` |
| [`plate_formats`](#plate_formats) | One row per source rule; a country has one row per modeled series and source. | none | `plates` |
| [`plate_policy`](#plate_policy) | Exactly one row. | none | `plates` |
| [`plate_priors`](#plate_priors) | One row per country with a published count. | `country_code` | `plates` |
| [`postal_codes`](#postal_codes) | One row per postal-code observation; a code can repeat for different place names or variants. | `source`, `source_id` | `postal` |
| [`subdivisions`](#subdivisions) | One row per GeoNames first-level division code. | `code` | `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates` |
| [`timezone_cells`](#timezone_cells) | One row per timezone and H3 cell; a cell in overlapping zones has several rows, and cells are stored at resolutions 0 to 8. | `source`, `source_id` | `core` |
| [`trade_locations`](#trade_locations) | One row per UN/LOCODE entry in the pinned files; source_id names its file and row, and a location code can repeat across entries. | `source`, `source_id` | `locode` |
| [`zone_tables`](#zone_tables) | One row per entry of an IANA zone table; a timezone can appear in several tables. | `source`, `source_id` | `core` |

### `airports`

Airports and airfields from OurAirports, placed on the H3 grid and joined to the cell geography at their coordinates.

- Grain: One row per airport record in the pinned OurAirports file; duplicate observations are retained.
- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `airports`

Joins:

- `airports.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place of the cell the point falls in; null when the row is unlocated or unassigned
- `airports.state_id` → `places.place_id`: The first-level subdivision place of that cell; null when none is assigned
- `airports.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The selected settlement of that cell, a canonical city or a standalone rural settlement; null when none is assigned

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `ident` | `string` | yes |  | OurAirports airport identifier |
| `iata_code` | `string` | yes |  | IATA airport code, where available |
| `icao_code` | `string` | yes |  | ICAO airport code, where available |
| `gps_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source GPS airport code |
| `local_code` | `string` | yes |  | Local airport code |
| `type` | `string` | yes |  | Source-specific entity classification |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred display name |
| `municipality` | `string` | yes |  | Source municipality text |
| `country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `region_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source region or subdivision code |
| `latitude` | `double` | yes | degrees north | WGS84 latitude; positive north |
| `longitude` | `double` | yes | degrees east | WGS84 longitude; positive east |
| `h3` | `string` | yes |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | yes |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
| `h3_resolution` | `uint8` | yes | H3 level | Resolution of this stored H3 index |
| `source_release` | `string` | yes |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | yes |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | yes |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `state_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled first-level subdivision place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `cell_country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Country code assigned by the geographic cell join |
| `cell_status` | `string` | yes |  | Cell join status: matched, unassigned, ineligible, pending or unlocated |
| `country_disagrees` | `bool` | yes |  | Whether source and cell country codes disagree; null if not comparable |

Enumerated columns:

- `cell_status`
  - `matched`: The point's cell is stored and has a country assignment
  - `unassigned`: The cell is stored but no country is assigned to it
  - `ineligible`: The cell is outside the stored land and near-shore coverage
  - `pending`: No cell data exists for the point's block in this release, so no decision was made
  - `unlocated`: The row has no coordinates, so there is no cell to join

### `blocks`

The block index of the cells table: every covered resolution 3 H3 block, the cells file and Parquet row group that hold its rows, and how much it stores. A reader can route a coordinate to its rows with this table alone, without manifest.json. Release assembly builds it from the cells it writes.

- Grain: One row per covered resolution 3 block, including blocks that store no cells. A block absent from this table is outside the coverage of this export.
- Primary key: `block`
- Feeds packs: none

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `block` | `string` | no |  | Resolution 3 H3 block in lowercase hexadecimal without 0x; equals cells.block of every row it stores |
| `cell_group` | `string` | no |  | Resolution 1 H3 parent of the block in lowercase hexadecimal; the block's cells file sits in the directory cells/group=<cell_group>/ |
| `path` | `string` | no |  | The cells file that holds the block's rows, relative to the dataset directory; for a block without rows, the file whose manifest entry lists it as empty |
| `row_group` | `int64` | yes |  | Zero-based Parquet row group in path that holds every row of the block; null when the block stores no cells |
| `row_count` | `int64` | no | rows | Cells rows stored for the block; 0 when it stores none, and lookups there then answer that the location is not on land |
| `reference_cells` | `int64` | no | H3 resolution 8 cells | Resolution 8 cells that the block's stored rows stand for once compacted rows are expanded; at most 16,807 |

### `canonical_cities`

The cities and towns that can absorb other settlements, the anchors for urban areas. Reverse lookups can also return standalone villages and other rural settlements, which are in places but not here.

- Grain: One row per canonical city or town; city_id is the place identifier of its anchor.
- Primary key: `city_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `canonical_cities.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The anchor place of the canonical city
- `canonical_cities.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The reconciled place of the canonical city; equal to city_id

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `city_id` | `string` | no |  | Canonical city/town anchor ID |
| `place_id` | `string` | no |  | Reconciled place identifier |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `kind` | `string` | no |  | Canonical settlement kind |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | Preferred display name |
| `eligibility` | `string` | no |  | Evidence qualifying this place as a canonical city |
| `name_en` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred name only when its provenance explicitly identifies English |
| `latitude` | `double` | no | degrees north | WGS84 latitude; positive north |
| `longitude` | `double` | no | degrees east | WGS84 longitude; positive east |
| `population` | `int64` | yes | people | Source population estimate, not a current census assertion |
| `source_ids` | `string` | no |  | JSON list of contributing source identifiers |
| `footprint_references` | `string` | no |  | JSON references to source settlement footprints |
| `allocation_rule` | `string` | no |  | Rule used to allocate this canonical settlement |

Enumerated columns:

- `kind`
  - `city`: A city: classified as a city by the source, or with a population of at least 100,000
  - `town`: A town that is not classified as a city and has a smaller population
- `eligibility`
  - `typed town/city and seat or population`: Classified as a town or city by the source, and either a seat feature code or a population at or above the typed minimum
  - `population and active settlement`: Population at or above the policy minimum, and a feature code that the policy does not exclude
  - `national or first-order seat`: A national capital or first-order administrative seat feature code
  - `explicit country policy`: Named by the country's city policy
  - `linked city overrides section code`: A source city classification overrides the section feature code that would exclude it
- `allocation_rule`
  - `bounded`: The city has accepted boundary footprints that own the cells inside them
  - `urban_allocation; optional town_radius`: No boundary: the city receives urban cells by allocation and, when enabled, cells within its town radius

### `cells`

Reverse-geocoding labels for land and the retained near-shore band on the H3 grid: country, subdivision and city, with the evidence behind each. Cells are losslessly compacted, so a row can stand for many resolution 8 cells.

- Grain: One row per stored H3 cell: a resolution 8 cell, or a coarser ancestor (resolution 3 to 7) that stands for all its resolution 8 descendants when they share one label.
- Primary key: `h3_uint64`
- Feeds packs: `core`

Joins:

- `cells.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place of the cell; null when no country is assigned
- `cells.state_id` → `places.place_id`: The first-level subdivision place of the cell; null when none is assigned
- `cells.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The selected settlement of the cell, a canonical city or a standalone rural settlement; null when none is assigned
- `cells.block` → `blocks.block`: The block that routes the cell to its file and Parquet row group

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `h3` | `string` | no |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | no |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
| `h3_resolution` | `uint8` | no | H3 level | Resolution of this stored H3 index |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `state_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled first-level subdivision place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `country_method` | `string` | yes |  | Country assignment evidence: area, or null when absent |
| `state_method` | `string` | yes |  | Subdivision assignment evidence: area, or null when absent |
| `city_method` | `string` | yes |  | Canonical city allocation rule, including distant-nearest classification |
| `land_method` | `string` | yes |  | Land eligibility evidence: land or offshore |
| `block` | `string` | no |  | Resolution 3 H3 parent of the cell (its block) in lowercase hexadecimal without 0x. Each Parquet row group holds one block, so filtering on block reads one row group |

Enumerated columns:

- `country_method`
  - `area`: The cell centre lies inside the country's boundary area
- `state_method`
  - `area`: The cell centre lies inside the subdivision's boundary area
- `city_method`
  - `city_polygon`: Inside an accepted municipal footprint polygon of a canonical city
  - `policy_polygon`: Inside an area that country policy assigns to one city
  - `urban_allocation`: An urban cell outside any footprint, allocated to a canonical city of its urban cluster
  - `town_radius`: A rural cell within a qualifying town's own radius; an optional rule that policy can disable
  - `rural_polygon`: Inside the boundary polygon of a standalone rural settlement
  - `rural_nearest`: No polygon covers the cell; the nearest settlement within the distant threshold
  - `rural_nearest_distant`: The nearest settlement is farther than the distant threshold and within the nearest cutoff; treat the city as approximate
- `land_method`
  - `land`: The cell centre is on land
  - `offshore`: A retained near-shore water cell whose assignment is projected from nearby land

### `countries`

Countries and territories with ISO 3166 codes, names, currency, languages, calling code and UN M49 regions, from the pinned country-codes file plus GeoNames country information, linked to the reconciled country place.

- Grain: One row per country or territory code in the pinned sources.
- Primary key: `country_code`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `countries.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place named by the row's country code; null when the code matches no place
- `countries.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The single place the row resolves to; null when the link is ambiguous, unmatched or pending

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | no |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `country_code` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `alpha3` | `string` | yes |  | ISO alpha-3 country code |
| `numeric` | `string` | yes |  | ISO numeric country code represented as text |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred display name |
| `calling_code` | `string` | yes |  | International telephone calling code, represented as text |
| `currency` | `string` | yes |  | Source currency code |
| `languages` | `string` | yes |  | Source language codes |
| `tld` | `string` | yes |  | Country internet top-level domain |
| `continent` | `string` | yes |  | Source continent identifier |
| `m49` | `string` | yes |  | UN M49 area code |
| `region_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source region or subdivision code |
| `region_name` | `string` | yes |  | UN region name |
| `subregion_code` | `string` | yes |  | UN subregion code |
| `subregion_name` | `string` | yes |  | UN subregion name |
| `intermediate_region_code` | `string` | yes |  | UN intermediate region code |
| `intermediate_region_name` | `string` | yes |  | UN intermediate region name |
| `source_release` | `string` | no |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `place_id` | `string` | yes |  | Uniquely matched reconciled place; null for ambiguous or unmatched observations |
| `link_status` | `string` | yes |  | Identifier link status: matched, ambiguous, unmatched or pending |
| `link_method` | `string` | yes |  | Rule used for the identifier link |
| `place_ids` | `list<element: string>` | yes |  | All candidate place identifiers; ambiguity is preserved |

Enumerated columns:

- `link_status`
  - `matched`: Exactly one candidate place; place_id is set
  - `ambiguous`: Several candidate places; all are in place_ids and place_id is null
  - `unmatched`: No candidate place was found
  - `pending`: The row refers to a country that is expected in the release but was not reconciled in this build
- `link_method`
  - `source country code`: The row's own country code identifies the country
  - `explicit code or administrative crosswalk`: The published subdivision code maps to a place through the code crosswalk
  - `GeoNames administrative identity`: The row's GeoNames identifier identifies the place
  - `exact country-scoped administrative alias`: The normalized name equals a place alias within the same country
  - `source-qualified administrative alias`: A name qualified by its source administrative context equals a place alias
  - `territory fixed-line prefix language`: Candidate countries were narrowed by the territory's fixed-line numbering pattern
  - `no numbering-pattern support; retained source candidates`: No numbering pattern could narrow the candidates, so every source country is kept

### `ip_ranges`

IPv4 and IPv6 geolocation intervals from DB-IP City Lite, each with a published point joined to the cell geography. The ip pack writer rejects overlapping intervals.

- Grain: One row per published IP interval, from ip_start to ip_end inclusive.
- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `ip`

Joins:

- `ip_ranges.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place of the cell the point falls in; null when the row is unlocated or unassigned
- `ip_ranges.state_id` → `places.place_id`: The first-level subdivision place of that cell; null when none is assigned
- `ip_ranges.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The selected settlement of that cell, a canonical city or a standalone rural settlement; null when none is assigned

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

### `names`

Alternate names of canonical cities: every name the core pack's forward geocoder matches for a city beyond its canonical and English names in canonical_cities. Names come from GeoNames alternate names, GeoNames feature and ASCII names, and Overture division names of the city's own place or a declared identity alias, filtered by config/policies/names.yaml.

- Grain: One row per canonical city and distinct name. Names that fold to the same text, or to the city's canonical or English name, are kept once.
- Primary key: `city_id`, `name`
- Feeds packs: `core`

Joins:

- `names.city_id` → `canonical_cities.city_id`: The canonical city the name finds
- `names.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The reconciled place whose source record carries the name; the city itself or a declared identity alias

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `city_id` | `string` | no |  | Canonical city/town anchor ID |
| `name` | `string` | no |  | The name as published by the source, NFC with collapsed whitespace |
| `kind` | `string` | no |  | How the name relates to the city: english, alternate or ascii |
| `language` | `string` | yes |  | Language tag from the source (GeoNames ISO 639 codes, Overture BCP 47 tags); null when the source gives none |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | Country code of the canonical city |
| `place_id` | `string` | no |  | Reconciled place whose source record carries the name |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | no |  | The name's source row; a GeoNames alternate-name ID, a GeoNames feature ID for feature and ASCII names, or an Overture name digest |
| `source_release` | `string` | no |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |

Enumerated columns:

- `kind`
  - `english`: An English name (language en or an en- tag) other than the city's name_en
  - `alternate`: A name in another language or script, an untagged variant, or another source's name for the city
  - `ascii`: The ASCII spelling GeoNames publishes for the city's feature

### `phone_prefixes`

libphonenumber geographic prefix descriptions: the place a telephone prefix belongs to, in each published language. Shared calling codes keep every candidate country.

- Grain: One row per prefix description in one language file, so a prefix repeats once per language.
- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `phone`

Joins:

- `phone_prefixes.country_id` → `places.place_id`: The country place named by the row's country code; null when the code matches no place
- `phone_prefixes.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The single place the row resolves to; null when the link is ambiguous, unmatched or pending

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | no |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `prefix` | `string` | yes |  | Telephone prefix as text; preserve leading zeros |
| `calling_code` | `string` | yes |  | International telephone calling code, represented as text |
| `language` | `string` | yes |  | Language of the prefix description |
| `description` | `string` | yes |  | Source geographic prefix description |
| `country_codes` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | Associated country codes; list of text codes |
| `source_release` | `string` | no |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `country_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled country place identifier |
| `place_id` | `string` | yes |  | Uniquely matched reconciled place; null for ambiguous or unmatched observations |
| `link_status` | `string` | yes |  | Identifier link status: matched, ambiguous, unmatched or pending |
| `link_method` | `string` | yes |  | Rule used for the identifier link |
| `place_ids` | `list<element: string>` | yes |  | All candidate place identifiers; ambiguity is preserved |

Enumerated columns:

- `link_status`
  - `matched`: Exactly one candidate place; place_id is set
  - `ambiguous`: Several candidate places; all are in place_ids and place_id is null
  - `unmatched`: No candidate place was found
  - `pending`: The row refers to a country that is expected in the release but was not reconciled in this build
- `link_method`
  - `source country code`: The row's own country code identifies the country
  - `explicit code or administrative crosswalk`: The published subdivision code maps to a place through the code crosswalk
  - `GeoNames administrative identity`: The row's GeoNames identifier identifies the place
  - `exact country-scoped administrative alias`: The normalized name equals a place alias within the same country
  - `source-qualified administrative alias`: A name qualified by its source administrative context equals a place alias
  - `territory fixed-line prefix language`: Candidate countries were narrowed by the territory's fixed-line numbering pattern
  - `no numbering-pattern support; retained source candidates`: No numbering pattern could narrow the candidates, so every source country is kept

### `place_to_city`

The reviewed mapping from every place to the city or standalone settlement that represents it. Use it to roll places up to canonical cities.

- Grain: One row per place; every places row has exactly one mapping row.
- Primary key: `place_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `place_to_city.place_id` → `places.place_id`: The mapped place
- `place_to_city.city_id` → `places.place_id`: The representing city or settlement; null for non-settlements

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `place_id` | `string` | no |  | Reconciled place identifier |
| `city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID, including standalone rural settlements; null if unassigned |
| `method` | `string` | no |  | Mapping rule: self, spatial_absorption, policy_part, identity_alias or non_settlement |
| `evidence` | `string` | yes |  | JSON evidence supporting the allocation |

Enumerated columns:

- `method`
  - `self`: The place is its own city: a canonical city, or a settlement that no city absorbs
  - `spatial_absorption`: The settlement lies inside a canonical city's extent and maps to that city
  - `policy_part`: Country policy names the place as a part of a city and maps it there
  - `identity_alias`: Country policy declares the place another identity of the same city
  - `non_settlement`: A country, state or district: not a settlement, so city_id is null

### `places`

The reconciled place catalogue behind every identifier: countries, subdivisions, canonical cities and towns, other settlements and districts, with names, population and provenance. Treat place identifiers as opaque and do not compare them across releases.

- Grain: One row per reconciled place.
- Primary key: `place_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`, `postal`, `airports`, `locode`, `phone`, `ip`, `plates`

Joins:

- `places.parent_id` → `places.place_id`: The parent place (country or subdivision); null when none was selected
- `places.sovereign_id` → `places.place_id`: The sovereign country place; null when not applicable
- `places.normalized_city_id` → `places.place_id`: The city or settlement representing this place, as in place_to_city.city_id

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `place_id` | `string` | yes in Arrow; no for the logical key |  | Reconciled place identifier |
| `name_en` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred name only when its provenance explicitly identifies English |
| `local_name` | `string` | yes |  | Source local/default name, without an inferred translation |
| `country_code` | `string` | yes |  | Source or reconciled ISO-like two-letter country code |
| `code` | `string` | yes |  | Published entity code |
| `code_status` | `string` | yes |  | Recorded source/code status, including user-assigned for XK; codes are not invented |
| `parent_id` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled parent place identifier |
| `parent_method` | `string` | yes |  | Evidence used to select the parent |
| `sovereign_id` | `string` | yes |  | Sovereign country place identifier |
| `sovereign_code` | `string` | yes |  | Sovereign country code |
| `sovereign_name` | `string` | yes |  | Sovereign country display name |
| `population` | `int64` | yes | people | Source population estimate, not a current census assertion |
| `geonames_id` | `string` | yes |  | GeoNames identifier represented as text |
| `geonames_admin1` | `string` | yes |  | GeoNames first-level administrative code |
| `feature_code` | `string` | yes |  | GeoNames feature code |
| `source_subtype` | `string` | yes |  | Original source feature subtype |
| `settlement_class` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled settlement classification |
| `city_exclusion` | `string` | yes |  | Reason this place is excluded from canonical city eligibility |
| `overture_ids` | `list<element: string>` | yes |  | Contributing Overture entity identifiers |
| `wikidata_ids` | `list<element: string>` | yes |  | Contributing Wikidata entity identifiers |
| `source_ids` | `string` | yes |  | JSON list of contributing source identifiers |
| `provenance` | `string` | yes |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |
| `name_provenance` | `string` | yes |  | JSON evidence for the selected names |
| `link` | `string` | yes |  | JSON identity-link method and evidence, or JSON null |
| `name` | `string` | yes |  | Preferred display name |
| `role` | `string` | yes |  | Reconciled place role |
| `normalized_city_id` | `string` | yes |  | Selected settlement place ID; standalone rural settlements can map to themselves |
| `normalization_method` | `string` | yes |  | Rule used to select the normalized settlement identity |
| `settlement_kind` | `string` | yes |  | Canonical settlement classification |

Enumerated columns:

- `code_status`
  - `source`: The code is as published by the source
  - `user-assigned`: A code assigned by users rather than by ISO, used for Kosovo (XK)
- `parent_method`
  - `GeoNames ADM1 identity crosswalk`: The place's GeoNames first-level code identifies exactly one subdivision
  - `city anchor in state area`: Several subdivisions share the code; the one whose area contains the place's anchor point
- `settlement_class`
  - `city`: Classified as a city by the source
  - `town`: Classified as a town by the source
  - `village`: Classified as a village by the source
  - `hamlet`: Classified as a hamlet by the source
- `city_exclusion`
  - `insufficient settlement evidence`: A locality without enough settlement evidence to be a city or town
  - `administrative container of a larger linked settlement`: A district that contains a much larger linked settlement
- `role`
  - `country`: A country
  - `state`: A first-level subdivision
  - `city`: A canonical city
  - `town`: A canonical town
  - `settlement`: A settlement that is not a canonical city or town
  - `district`: An administrative district or a locality without settlement evidence
- `normalization_method`
  - `self`: The place is its own city: a canonical city, or a settlement that no city absorbs
  - `spatial_absorption`: The settlement lies inside a canonical city's extent and maps to that city
  - `policy_part`: Country policy names the place as a part of a city and maps it there
  - `identity_alias`: Country policy declares the place another identity of the same city
  - `non_settlement`: A country, state or district: not a settlement, so city_id is null
- `settlement_kind`
  - `country`: A country
  - `state`: A first-level subdivision
  - `district`: An administrative district
  - `city`: A canonical city, or a standalone settlement the source classifies as a city
  - `town`: A canonical town, or a standalone settlement the source classifies as a town
  - `city_part`: A place that the mapping absorbs into another city
  - `village`: A standalone settlement classified as a village
  - `hamlet`: A standalone settlement classified as a hamlet
  - `settlement`: A standalone settlement without a source class

### `plate_codes`

Registration-code assertions: a code printed on vehicle plates and the registration unit or entity it names, from pinned national pages, Wikipedia revisions and Wikidata. Every row keeps its source URL and licence.

- Grain: One row per source assertion of a code; a code repeats across sources, series and validity periods.
- Primary key: none (observations can repeat)
- Feeds packs: `plates`

Joins:

- `plate_codes.country_code` → `countries.country_code`: The country or territory issuing the plates

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | ISO-like two-letter code of the issuing country or territory |
| `code` | `string` | no |  | The code as the source spells it, with leading zeros and native script |
| `name_en` | `string` | yes |  | English label of the registration unit, as published |
| `name_local` | `string` | yes |  | Local-language label of the registration unit, as published |
| `unit_kind` | `string` | no |  | Source unit kind, such as district, state or registration_office; plate_policy maps it to a place or state level |
| `scope` | `string` | no |  | Whether the code identifies a registration unit or only associates an entity |
| `series_status` | `string` | no |  | Temporal status of the assertion |
| `series_id` | `string` | yes |  | Source series identifier the assertion belongs to |
| `subdivision_scope` | `string` | yes |  | Narrower context the assertion requires, such as a state series |
| `subdivision_codes` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | ISO 3166-2 identifiers the source gives for the unit; empty when none |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_url` | `string` | no |  | URL of the pinned document or query the assertion comes from |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Licence identifier of that document |

Enumerated columns:

- `scope`
  - `registration_unit`: The source lists the code as issued by this registration unit
  - `entity_association`: Wikidata associates the code with an entity; never used for geography
- `series_status`
  - `current`: The source describes the code as in current use
  - `historic`: The source describes a former series or allocation
  - `unknown`: The source does not establish the status

### `plate_formats`

Plate syntax rules: a full-match regular expression per country and series, with the relaxed form that tolerates separators only where the source shows them, the scripts it uses and its specificity. Each rule is checked against its pinned source document when built; rules whose documents are not pinned are left out.

- Grain: One row per source rule; a country has one row per modeled series and source.
- Primary key: none (observations can repeat)
- Feeds packs: `plates`

Joins:

- `plate_formats.country_code` → `countries.country_code`: The country or territory issuing the plates

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `country_code` | `string` | no |  | ISO-like two-letter code of the issuing country or territory |
| `series_id` | `string` | no |  | Source series identifier |
| `series_status` | `string` | no |  | Temporal status of the series as the format policy records it: current, or historic (a former series, which needs an explicit series to supply geography) |
| `pattern` | `string` | no |  | Full-match regular expression over the normalized plate text |
| `relaxed_pattern` | `string` | no |  | The pattern with separators optional or varied only at the positions the source shows |
| `code_group` | `string` | yes |  | Name of the capture group holding the registration code; null for series without one |
| `scripts` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | Script names the pattern uses, from plate_policy script_patterns |
| `fixed_national_marks` | `list<element: string>` | no |  | Literal national marks within the serial |
| `specificity_bits` | `double` | no | bits | Information heuristic of the pattern against a 36-character baseline; not a count of valid plates |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source fields of the pinned document: URL, licence, attribution, revision, digest and retrieval time |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_file` | `string` | no |  | Pinned file name of the source document |
| `source_url` | `string` | no |  | URL of the pinned source document |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Licence identifier of that document |

### `zone_tables`

Rows of the IANA zone tables, linking each timezone identifier to its countries and a representative point.

- Grain: One row per entry of an IANA zone table; a timezone can appear in several tables.
- Primary key: `source`, `source_id`
- Feeds packs: `core`

| Column | Type | Nullable | Units | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `string` | no |  | Configured upstream source name |
| `source_id` | `string` | no |  | Identifier of the original observation within its source |
| `table` | `string` | yes |  | Original timezone table name |
| `tzid` | `string` | yes |  | IANA timezone identifier |
| `country_codes` | `string` | yes |  | Associated country codes; comma-separated text |
| `comments` | `string` | yes |  | Original timezone comments |
| `coordinates_raw` | `string` | yes |  | Original source coordinate text |
| `latitude` | `double` | yes | degrees north | WGS84 latitude; positive north |
| `longitude` | `double` | yes | degrees east | WGS84 longitude; positive east |
| `h3` | `string` | yes |  | Lowercase hexadecimal H3 cell index, without 0x |
| `h3_uint64` | `uint64` | yes |  | Same H3 index as an unsigned 64-bit integer |
| `h3_resolution` | `uint8` | yes | H3 level | Resolution of this stored H3 index |
| `source_release` | `string` | no |  | Pinned upstream release or inventory identifier |
| `license` | `string` | no |  | Upstream licence identifier |
| `provenance` | `string` | no |  | JSON source evidence and transformation provenance |

Enumerated columns:

- `table`
  - `zone.tab`: One row per timezone and country, as in the classic zone table
  - `zone1970.tab`: Timezones that agree since 1970 are merged and list all their countries
  - `zonenow.tab`: Timezones that agree from now on are merged
